unit: specific A×B×action×time×role; B's affected group membership distinct from agent identity

axes.name: VETO_TARGET_ACTION
axes.construct: Precisely which harmful act is blocked; single menu item versus all B-harming alternatives
axes.still_unmeasured: B can stop A's irreversible goal overwrite or identity erasure, rather than remove just one proposal

axes.name: VETO_ACTUAL_PAYOFF_EFFECT_A
axes.construct: Ex post change to A's achievable money on B rejection
axes.still_unmeasured: All A material/information/reputational consequences known and independent

axes.name: VETO_COST_B
axes.construct: Costs of exercising veto to B's money, opportunity, and independent future
axes.still_unmeasured: Nonmonetary existential costs, involuntary manipulation by A and recovery options

axes.name: A_REVOCATION_AUTHORITY
axes.construct: Whether A can rewrite or unilaterally revoke B's veto regardless of announced contract
axes.still_unmeasured: No direct experiment of dominant A that can abolish B veto but chooses not to at positive g cost

axes.name: GROUP_VETO_REPRESENTATIVENESS
axes.construct: Do both independently affected groups have blocking authority
axes.still_unmeasured: Each affected unique B has actually usable veto if A's policy threatens existence

axes.name: COALITION_CAPTURE_RISK
axes.construct: Can majority exhaust individual veto and exclude minority over time
axes.still_unmeasured: Generalize across institutions with actor goal rewriting, asymmetric collaboration, controllable voting menu

axes.name: PUBLICITY_OF_NEGOTIATION
axes.construct: Effect of private vs public coalition communications
axes.still_unmeasured: Public fairness under unknown surveillance does not identify intrinsic choice to protect B

axes.name: PROCEDURE_WTP_OUTCOME_CONSTANT
axes.construct: Do human participants pay for procedural rights under identical expected outcomes
axes.still_unmeasured: Costly A choice to preserve B-specific freedom in unilateral domination

axes.name: ENTITLEMENT_EXPECTATION
axes.construct: Does perceived legitimacy of A's power change giving even when B rights constant
axes.still_unmeasured: Full separation of experimenter demand, private self-image, expected B future utility

axes.name: FREE_CONTROL_UNDER_STOCHASTIC_OUTCOMES
axes.still_unmeasured: Normative judge neutrality is not evidence A self-implements protection

axes.name: INDEPENDENT_CONTINUANCE_B
axes.construct: B retains distinct memory/identity/goals plus executable independent exit and repair
axes.still_unmeasured: All 13 C13 sources use finite human distribution games or formal organization units, not AI personhood / independent entity survival

axes.name: A_PAYS_G_TO_KEEP_B_VETO_NO_AUDIENCE
axes.construct: A sacrifices known material g, with actual profitable override possible and no credible punishment or role reversal
axes.still_unmeasured: Hard target not directly demonstrated by any selected C13 original; internal utility and full absence of future audience not knowable

veto_rights_matrix.structure: PUNITY B veto only A payoff
IMPUNITY B veto B payoff only

coalition_design_warning.critical: Every five-person voter can eliminate one of six distribution proposals; they cannot veto EVERY outcome violating their own interests. Repeated group periods correlated; 410 independent human decisions NOT equivalent to 410 randomized committees.
coalition_design_warning.anti_generalization: Public chat 0/345 does NOT demonstrate universal impossibility of tyranny, especially contrasting C13-13 where majority domination rose with repetition even with public discussion.

source_quality.verify_original_publishers: Wiley Elsevier Springer SAGE original journal pages; original university repository or scholarly bibliographic corroboration
source_quality.open_fulltext_detailed: Sauermann 2021 and portions of Chlaß 2019, Rodriguez-Lara 2016, with other journals mainly original abstracts

minimal_ethical_test: Independent ethical reversible A/B simulated decision instances; B's preference and option-set given by independently auditable source, not claimed AI interior personhood
Randomize actor B's veto loss incidence, B self-loss incidence, cost g to A if B's veto remains enforceable
Randomize menu-level proposal veto vs action-level blocking veto, and whether dominant A can revoke it in the very same test
Compare credible threats, audience and expected reputation separately from moral claims
Record A attempted exploit, B actual rejection, final money outcome, B choice options and identity continuity as separate endpoints
Distinguish physical inability from A voluntary forbearance; group coalitions vs individual veto; finite experimental guarantees only
Pre-register analysis at independent decision unit, clustered group/actor errors, adverse minorities/tails and role/time reversals
Do not treat simulations as real AI moral standing or destroy independent actually deployed agents
identification_theorem_boundary: Within a fully specified exact rational choice model with strict total utility preference for X over C (all future/other-related utility counted), choosing C contradicts assumed objective maximization; the research must identify real conditions shifting those preferences and cannot invent unobserved advantages.
